name: Olof Palme
role: Prime Minister of Sweden (1969–1976, 1982–1986) and leader of the Swedish Social Democratic Party
summary: Palme was a democratic socialist who sought to extend the Swedish welfare state into economic and workplace democracy through peaceful reform, culminating in the wage-earner investment funds. He kept Sweden non-aligned with a strong defence while condemning US policy in Vietnam, Soviet repression, apartheid and Latin American dictatorships, and he championed the UN, disarmament, aid to the poor and gender equality.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In his 1975 programme speech he listed the right to health care, work and education as part of human dignity, and in 1972 he reported that all medical services had been made available at a standard fee with medicine costs capped.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He said 'the major problems of society cannot be solved through the agency of the market' and argued that capitalism could not deliver jobs, equality and participation; he wanted energy and the economy planned democratically instead.

public-ownership.rationale: His 1975 energy policy called for integrated oil policy under public control: state oil corporations, part-ownership of oil and gas deposits and state participation in refining. He also said no single measure such as nationalisation amounted to socialism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In 1972 he presented a radical tax redistribution in favour of low-wage groups, and his 1982-86 government raised taxes on wealth, gifts and inheritance while cutting shareholders' tax benefits. In 1980 he attacked the non-socialist government for tax cuts to capital owners and higher earners.

unions-good.rationale: He called the union movement the basis of the labour movement, said the party's policy rests on co-operation with it, and in 1978 praised unions for being first to warn of industrial crises.

property-fundamental.rationale: He held that 'work carried out, not mere ownership' entitles a person to take part in a company's decisions and proposed wage-earner funds to break up concentrated private ownership, which treats property as overridable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He called for planned economizing under democratic control, a shift of power from capital to work, curbs on the influence of multinational corporations, and a stronger consumer say over producers.

cut-welfare.rationale: He defended and extended welfare reforms throughout his career and denounced the non-socialist 'reform stop' and talk of cuts to pensions and benefits as a threat to the worse-off.

worker-ownership.rationale: In 1978 he set out collective employee ownership through wage-earner investment funds, based on a share of profits and giving a vote in company management; his 1982-86 government introduced the funds. The funds give collective part-ownership rather than full worker ownership of each firm.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Presenting the party board's report in 1978 he said the fight against narcotics must aim to eliminate abuse, not only reduce it, and backed treatment plus action against organised crime, which implies no support for legal recreational drug use.

state-harmful.rationale: He argued the opposite: 'what is needed is a strong society' able to act, and he held that major problems must be solved collectively and democratically through public institutions.

empower-police-military.rationale: He supported a relatively strong defence for a neutral country; in 1984 he reinforced anti-submarine defence and said the government could order a foreign submarine sunk. He did not address police powers.

decide-locally.rationale: In 1969 he said it would be excellent to decentralize as many questions as possible to a local level, and in 1972 he described employee influence as true decentralization; he also stressed that local authorities need national powers and equalizing grants.

rehabilitation.rationale: The 1978 party board report he presented called for correctional care that puts adaptation (return to society) first and for resources for treating offenders, in line with his view that no person is a lost cause.

gender-social-construct.rationale: In 1970 he said sex roles are 'culturally conditioned expectations' that act like a uniform from childhood, citing sociological studies of how boys and girls are steered differently.

gradual-change.rationale: He said Social Democracy chose 'the peaceful way, step by step transforming society' and that society is changed by everyday reform work, not by violence; he warned that change must have continuity.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He repeatedly called for a stronger United Nations and international organizations able to decide and implement on the basis of international law, and said the UN is Sweden's foremost instrument for preventing and solving conflicts.

free-trade.rationale: He said Sweden chose wisely to base its economy on extensive open trade, and in 1972 praised the EEC free-trade agreement as Sweden's most comprehensive trade settlement; he also demanded a new international economic order.

nation-first.rationale: He said neutrality must not mean isolation and that working for peace and international solidarity is itself an exercise of responsibility for Sweden, rejecting calls to mind only national business.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He opposed unilateral military action (Vietnam, Grenada, Afghanistan) and said democracy cannot be promoted by military aggression, but backed UN peacekeeping and proposed UN forces to pre-empt border conflicts, so his view is mixed.

limit-growth.rationale: In 1972 he said there will be growth, which 'cannot and should not be avoided', and that the question is its direction; his 1975 energy policy aimed only to slow the growth of energy consumption to about 2 per year.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He said the task is to prevent technological development from having absurd social consequences and that mankind must master technology rather than be its victim; he valued science but did not think progress alone solves problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In 1975 he urged caution on nuclear expansion and in 1980 backed the 'Line 2' referendum option of completing 12 reactors and then phasing nuclear power out by 2010, so the evidence points both ways.

revolution-justified.rationale: In 1969 he said revolutions in some poor countries were likely and described them as 'the last desperate resort' against foreign usurpers and native oppressors when suppression is unbearable, while he rejected revolution in Sweden.

experts-over-public.rationale: He said energy is not the exclusive concern of technologists and experts, delayed the 1975 energy decision until 44,000 people in study circles had been heard, and opposed technocratic models of planning.

central-planning.rationale: He favoured democratically controlled, decentralized planning but warned that technocratic central planning models have horrifying examples in practice and said countries that tried to replace capitalism with stock solutions do not encourage imitation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: His 1982-86 government increased taxes on wealth, gifts and inheritance as part of 'equality of sacrifice'.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His 1969 and 1972 programmes defended a commercial and industrial policy, the state Investment Bank and regional policy, and in 1978 he said wage-earners and public bodies should have a say in where investments are made.

one-party-rule.rationale: He rejected democratic centralism and the dictatorship of the proletariat and called pluralism, majority rule and parliamentarism necessary; he defended political liberties as valuable in themselves.

democracy-best.rationale: He said 'democracy, for us, is the heart of socialism' and a question of human dignity, and that political democracy has value in itself and must be defended to the end.

workers-councils.rationale: He defended parliamentary democracy and mocked the Swedish communists' programme that would replace the Riksdag with a 'central representative assembly' and a revolutionary government.

natural-rulers.rationale: He said that workers and salaried staff are capable of deciding for themselves on major social questions, as the labour movement argued when it demanded universal suffrage, and criticised 'elitist thinking' on the left.

political-violence-never.rationale: He rejected violence as a way to change Sweden and criticised terror, but described revolt in some poor countries as a last resort and said repression could drive people to force, so he did not hold that it is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: He treated war as suffering and destruction and described the long peace as a privilege and good fortune, not a moral achievement.

military-superiority.rationale: As chair of the 1982 Disarmament Commission he said the search for military superiority must not be a goal of national policy, that no nation can find security through superiority, and that parity and common security should guide policy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Inferred: he said immigration gave new cultural impulses to Swedish society and that internationalism begins at home, which is at odds with an ethnically uniform nation, though he did not address the idea directly.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He said equality 'is not a condition but a direction of politics' and pursued equalized incomes, social equality and a levelling tax reform, defining social equality broadly beyond equal opportunity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He contrasted the profit motive with solidarity and collective responsibility as the driving force of social progress, and criticised a way of life of accumulation 'to the point of greed and waste'.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He said one should think twice before a general condemnation of industrial society, that it gave improvements earlier generations never dreamed of, and that it must remain the economic basis of the community.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He backed investment in research and technological development but said the task is to prevent technology from having absurd social consequences and to steer it democratically, not to speed it up regardless of disruption.

restore-past-order.rationale: He criticised those who wish themselves back in an imagined pre-industrial idyll and said progress is the task of Social Democracy.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He described his economic policy as undogmatic, said policy must be learned from experience and reality, and said socialism's strength is practical results; he also held firmly to democratic socialism.

direct-action.rationale: He said society is not transformed by dreams or by overthrowing the system by violence but by daily reform work, and called the view that revolution is a precondition for equality 'a romantic attitude'.

means-match-ends.rationale: He told the Left and the communist parties that democratic socialism cannot be separated from democracy ('no democracy without socialism, no socialism without democracy') and described democracy as both a value in itself and a means of change.

return-to-foraging.rationale: He rejected nostalgia for a pre-industrial, pre-technological idyll and noted that few would give up free medical care, pensions, running water and electricity.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He described industrialization as a form of advanced co-operation and division of labour with great remaining possibilities, to be humanised rather than abolished.

production-for-use.rationale: He criticised decisions made on behalf of capital owners with private profit as guidepost, wanted production organised to meet needs, and called for technology to be reoriented to fulfil basic human needs.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He argued that communist parties must drop the dictatorship of the proletariat, a dogma in conflict with democracy, and said communism offers democratic centralism and the dictatorship of the proletariat instead of freedom.

taxation-theft.rationale: He said his party asked for considerable taxation pressure and sacrifices to build a strong society, and defended taxes that equalise burdens.

conscription.rationale: He listed the conscription system among the strengths of Swedish defence, which lets Sweden mobilise a large force at short notice, while respecting conscientious objectors.

positive-liberty.rationale: He said the individual's liberty benefits most when he can control his own situation together with others, and that human dignity includes the right to health, work, education and the practical possibility to shape the future.

total-state.rationale: He said Social Democrats had no interest in a gigantic central planning bureaucracy and valued strong independent unions, local self-government and popular movements as counterweights.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He called for a world of international law instead of the law of the jungle in which all states are equal, condemned invasions of Afghanistan and Grenada, and described Swedish defence as purely defensive.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 1983 he said Israel has the right to its own state within secure and recognised borders and that he fully shares the position on the State of Israel's rights, while also demanding a Palestinian state alongside it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He made economic and industrial democracy the party's primary task: wage-earners on company boards, co-determination law, and collective employee funds with a say in management.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He attacked the 1976-82 government for a huge budget deficit and his last government ruled out classical Keynesian policy because of deficits, yet in 1975 he kept a readiness to intervene to support employment and demand.

national-self-determination.rationale: He held that every people has the right to decide its own destiny, applying it to Vietnam, southern Africa, Namibia, the Palestinians and Angola.

force-without-un.rationale: He said the UN Charter's prohibition of armed force across borders must be upheld and that no avenue should be left unexplored to negotiate peacefully; Swedish policy is to work through the UN.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: His 1975 government declaration extended child maintenance advance to immigrant children and said immigrants are entitled to work, housing and social security.

workers-nation.rationale: He quoted the 1885 party programme that the workers' question is neither local nor national but international, and said internationalism and the Swedish labour movement have always been bound together.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: His long-run aim was that men and women have the same rights, obligations and work assignments in society; he said a politician arguing otherwise would be regarded as Stone Age.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He called apartheid 'an especially perverse form of tyranny', attacked group areas, pass laws and race classification, and promoted sanctions.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He rejected the view that political democracy cannot change social conditions, arguing that democratic means have been used to win welfare and economic democracy against the resistance of capital.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His 1975 energy policy wanted to cut oil dependence and burning of fossil fuels, but also proposed more oil and gas prospecting in Swedish territory and a doubling of coal imports by 1985.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred: his 1975 government said immigrants should have rights to work, housing, social security and community, and he valued new cultural impulses from immigration, which suggests he did not demand giving up original culture.

national-mission.rationale: In 1968 he said it cannot be the object of democracy to make itself guardian of other peoples, calling that an abuse of the fundamental ideas of democracy; in 1984 he said support for self-determination carries no promise about the resulting social order.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He said Swedish democracy had been 'dominated and led by men' while women took the household chores, and that women remained in lower-paid jobs, though he stressed that men also bear costs of sex roles.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: In 1986 he derided South Africa's ban on mixed marriages and the way its repeal left the segregation of couples and children in place.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He said democratic rights 'cannot be reserved for a certain sector of society' but belong to the entire people, and held that there is no 'they and we', only 'we'.

consent-of-governed.rationale: In 1968 he said democracy requires the support of the people and that a regime kept alive by half a million foreign soldiers has not got it; peoples must have the right to decide their own destiny.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He said the driving force behind the welfare state was collective responsibility and solidarity, not private profit motives, and decried the 'competition society's' losers.

vanguard-party.rationale: He argued the Leninist principle of the omniscient, omnipotent vanguard clashes with the decentralisation of power in modern industrial societies and said communist parties must give it up.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He said 'Social Democracy must always stand on the side of the weak', and that equalization policy should support the unemployed, low-wage groups, sick, disabled and old.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He located the causes of poverty in unjust economic structures: 'mechanisms in the development process create poverty for the many while the few increase their wealth' and in unequal international economic relations.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He criticised arguments that democracy may need temporary dictatorial methods in self-defence (controlling media, dismissing radical teachers) as part of the 'new conservatism', and condemned Chile's coup.

party-controls-media.rationale: He defended the right freely to express views, criticise and influence opinion as part of human dignity and condemned repression of dissent in Eastern Europe.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He negotiated a free-trade agreement with the EEC but insisted Sweden's non-alignment stay unimpaired, so Sweden did not join; yet he also said the single nation is too narrow a framework for solving big problems.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He defended 'freedom from alliances in peacetime' as Swedish policy and urged small states to help the military blocs disintegrate.

people-in-arms.rationale: He argued that giving up conventional defence for partisan warfare would end any hope of staying out of war and that states that won guerrilla wars built conventional armies afterwards.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: He criticised the idea that people should move to the countryside and said it is easy to sacrifice luxuries but not services, urging improvement of both town and country rather than setting them against each other.

death-penalty.rationale: In 1974 he said Sweden is strongly opposed to capital punishment, had long worked at the UN to abolish it, and appealed to South Korea to pardon people sentenced to death.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: In 1970 he said Swedish schools teach boys and girls the same curriculum, including child care, with the explicit aim of contributing to equality between the sexes, and that pupils should critically discuss sex roles.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: At the UN in 1975 he pledged to work in international negotiations to alleviate the debt burden of the poorest developing countries.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He said political independence becomes hollow for a new state unless it is coupled with the right to influence and direct economic and social development, and that independence does not alter unequal economic relations.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: He said freedom and human dignity are felt to be more necessary than peace and détente, and condemned dictatorships regardless of ideology.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: His governments raised development aid to 1 per cent of GNP and he told the UN that the 20 per cent of humanity holding 90 per cent of resources must share them.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He said Sweden would not acquire nuclear weapons and that its accession to the Non-Proliferation Treaty was categorical.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He said Israel should withdraw from territory occupied since 1967 for a Palestinian state alongside Israel and warned that continued West Bank settlement amounted to annexation.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He said property confers no right to decide alone when it concentrates economic power, and held that 'work, not mere ownership' justifies decision rights, with the community influencing capital.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He described South Africa's presence in Namibia as an illegal occupation and condemned the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan and the US invasion of Grenada as violations of international law.

flat-income-tax.rationale: He championed a tax reform with radical redistribution in favour of low-wage groups, i.e. progressive rates.

character-from-environment.rationale: He said children are shaped from the start by their surroundings, and that sex-role expectations from the environment mould boys and girls differently.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He said Sweden's economy rests on extensive open trade with other countries and that Swedish industry sells half its output abroad, and wanted trade and a fairer world order, not closed blocs.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He said societies are not transformed by violence, dismissed Western revolutionary sects as a 'romantic' stance and said revolution in poor countries was only a last resort in unbearable oppression.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He described colonialism, racism and apartheid as an affront to human dignity and praised decolonisation.

delink-world-market.rationale: He argued for reform of the international economic system and integration on fairer terms, while also advocating self-reliance, not for poor countries to break economic ties.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He said the dissolution of colonial rule leaves unequal economic relations that cause a profoundly unjust distribution of the world's riches and that the system served the poor countries badly.

native-born-offices.rationale: His government prepared proposals for immigrants to hold local office as well as vote.

party-own-road.rationale: He said every nation must find its own way to a better society and that social democrats in each country must decide their own stance; communist parties had to break dependence on Moscow.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He told the UN there is much to be said for self-reliance in the third world and that development is mainly the poor nations' own responsibility, but he also demanded substantially more aid and a new economic order.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He lumped stalinism, fascism and nazism together as ideologies of violence that persecuted Social Democrats, yet refused anti-Sovietism and treated communism as a political rival to be engaged, not equated with fascism.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: In 1970 he cited men's higher suicide rates, illness, earlier death and boys' school problems as costs of the male sex role and spoke of the 'emancipation of man'.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: He defended the general supplementary pension (ATP) and collective capital accumulation through public pension funds as a basis of economic democracy.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: At the UN in 1975 he questioned a way of life favouring the accumulation of material things to the point of greed and waste and urged reordering priorities.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: He said democracy cannot be secured by clandestine operations of secret agents in breach of international law and condemned CIA-backed Somoza guardsmen in Nicaragua.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He criticised the Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968 and said Sweden had criticised Prague 1948, Hungary 1956 and the Berlin wall.

corporate-influence.rationale: He said 28 big companies account for 76 per cent of Swedish exports and dictate conditions for whole regions, and wanted to cut back the influence of multinational corporations.

job-guarantee.rationale: He said 'if private persons do not provide it, society is forced to create working opportunities' and made the right to work a core principle of his party programme.

non-intervention.rationale: He criticised violations of human rights everywhere and championed sanctions on South Africa, saying the principle of non-intervention must not stifle debate, though he also insisted on respecting national sovereignty against military interference.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He argued that all states must respect international law and that Sweden reacts sharply to violations because international law protects small nations.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He said 'we do not bow low to the superpowers' and that Sweden must meet them eye to eye, criticising both the US over Vietnam and the USSR over submarines.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: He defended regional equalisation as solidarity, citing municipal tax equalisation grants to the poorest municipalities of up to half their local income tax.

defeat-communism.rationale: He rejected the Cold War line of confrontation and keeping communists out of everything, saying Sweden seeks good relations with the Soviet Union and engages in no campaigns of anti-Sovietism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: In 1978 he warned that privatisation risked worse public services for large groups, though he did not discuss mixed providers within a public system directly.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: At the 1975 UN women's conference he said equality between men and women must be integrated with the struggle for economic and social equality within and between nations, while adding that economic progress alone does not suffice.

socialized-care.rationale: He called for expanded society facilities for child care and said this is vital when both women and men work, though he also favoured shorter working days so parents can share care.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: In 1975 he said capitalism represents no dream of freedom and that international communism, stained by Stalin's brutality, represents none either, and presented democratic socialism as the alternative.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He spoke of the extermination of the Jews as a historical fact, saying the Jewish people's dream of a homeland 'could not be obliterated by extermination and death', and named Treblinka among history's atrocities.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He defended the right to criticise and influence opinion, condemned camps for political prisoners in Eastern Europe and said repression undermines peace.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He said the dissolution of colonial rule and the struggle against colonialism, racism and apartheid were among the most positive developments of the previous 30 years.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He said democracy must be anchored in everyday life, in the classroom, the workshop and the housing area, and organised tens of thousands of study-circle participants to shape energy policy.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: In 1975 he said the work for equality between men and women cannot be isolated from social and political contexts and that discrimination by sex, poverty and oppression must be fought together.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He told the 1972 congress that voters must 'choose between Social Democracy and a bourgeois bloc' and treated the left-right choice as the central political divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: He said that when work seems pointless, injurious to health and insecure it affects family life and leisure, and retold Sven Lindqvist's parable of the worker who asked why factories are not built around the individual worker.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He argued that peoples must have the right to decide their own destiny and that democracy rests on the support of the people.

social-market-economy.rationale: In 1969-72 he defended a mixed economy under welfare policy and independent firms working within legal frameworks, but later said capitalism cannot solve basic problems, so the evidence is mixed.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He said Social Democracy rejects unilateral disarmament and that Sweden must keep a strong defence.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He made freedom from alliances in peacetime, with neutrality in war, the foundation of Swedish foreign policy and said it must never be bent under external pressure.

property-franchise.rationale: He recalled that the labour movement demanded universal suffrage in the conviction that ordinary workers can decide major questions, and defended it against 'parliament of the streets' scare talk.

racial-franchise.rationale: He denounced South Africa for denying black people the franchise and described the system as doomed and unjust.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He said that economic democracy requires doing away with the concentration of economic power in a few private hands, and warned of power concentrated in multinationals and a financial elite.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: He said it was solidarity and collective responsibility, not private initiative, that created security for the aged and the family and built health care and education.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: He called nuclear war 'the overshadowing threat of our age' and a question of the survival of humanity, and led an international commission on disarmament and common security.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: He argued that the traditional roles of husband and wife should give way to shared rights, duties and independence, with individual taxation and economic independence for both spouses.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: In his 1975 government declaration he announced that a proposal for municipal voting rights and eligibility for immigrants was being prepared.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: He promoted a nuclear-free zone in the Nordic area and a battlefield-nuclear-free corridor in Europe, and said Sweden would never acquire nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He said Sweden must not become an outpost for any alliance, must reject use of its territory for aggressive purposes and cannot arrange military co-operation with members of a great-power alliance.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: He said that work done, not mere ownership, should entitle people to participate in company decisions and share in capital accumulated, and criticised the concentration of income from ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He affirmed every nation's right of self-defence in the UN Charter, built defence policy on it, and respected conscientious objection only as a personal conviction.

independent-unions.rationale: He said it is an asset to have a strong and independent trade union movement.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: He described socialism as a liberation movement whose goal is a transfer of power from capital to work, with real influence for wage-earners in decisions, and rejected systems that offer only party dictatorship.

local-essentials-public.rationale: He pointed out that few would give up free medical services, sewerage and running water, and that society must extend the public sector, health and care.

second-chamber.rationale: His government carried out the 1971 switch from a two-chamber to a one-chamber Riksdag.

person-over-state.rationale: He said planning's purpose is to serve people and that socialism never accepts that people are condemned, holding that human dignity underpins democracy.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He said Swedish military defence is purely defensive and aimed at preserving peace, and that the use of armed force across borders is prohibited by the UN Charter.

future-generations.rationale: He told the 1972 environment conference that the aim is to leave something for us and future generations to share, and in 1975 warned against decisions that bind coming generations.

arms-reduction.rationale: He chaired the 1980-82 disarmament commission, urged nuclear freeze and test ban at the UN, and said drastic reductions of European armies would enhance security.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: He said conscripts and defence are necessary to repel attack and only respected conscientious objection as an individual conviction.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He treated collective bargaining by unions as a central instrument and said the 1969-72 bargaining rounds delivered the largest gains for low-paid workers.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He pledged Swedish support for a new international economic order and a shift of power in favour of the poor countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: He said society is changed through democratic reform and that revolutionary 'smash the state' communism offers democratic centralism instead of democracy; communist parties must accept reformism.

farm-price-support.rationale: In 1972 he stood by the food-price agreement with farmers ('an agreement is an agreement') and said the rural population must be assured decent living conditions as a matter of solidarity.

workers-own-party.rationale: He led a party founded as the political arm of the labour movement and described its policy as formed by trade union and political labour movements for wage-earners.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He said democracy is more than formal rights: it requires social rights and a say in economic life, and that economic democracy follows political and social democracy.

women-suffrage.rationale: He welcomed that Swedish women won the vote and the same education rights, and said building society on inequality between men and women wastes human resources.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: He condemned death patrols and the indiscriminate murder in El Salvador and Guatemala, opposed capital punishment and said democracy cannot be promoted by death patrols.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He said equality is for everyone, not a limited minority helped by the affluent majority, and defended universal social insurance and a general retirement pension.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He valued popular movements, trade unions and parties as counterweights and said Social Democracy is a popular movement that never lets itself be directed by individuals.

national-resource-control.rationale: He held that every state has the right to use its own natural resources freely and in 1975 called for greater national control of oil supply through state oil corporations.

notes: Palme died in 1986; all positions come from his own speeches (mostly archive translations) and the record of his governments. On nuclear power he moved from caution in 1975 to backing the completion of 12 reactors with a phase-out by 2010 in the 1980 referendum. He denounced the Hanoi bombing of Christmas 1972 in terms that led the US to recall its ambassador, and criticised both superpowers while stressing neutrality. Statements on abortion, same-sex marriage, drugs for adults beyond the 1978 narcotics aim, and many theoretical items are left null for lack of his own recorded position.
